note: The people who live in the open world's town buildings (core/game/game_villagers.gd, drawn by the sandbox screen when a house has its roof off; checked by tools/check_data.gd). A plain house holds as many residents as its floor has room for: each needs `area_per_person` tiles times their size squared (`sizes`: a halfling is 0.75 of a human, an orc 1.2; `monsters` are creatures that live beside the people of a town, `monster_percent` of the places, and only in a house with the room for them: an ogre wants 26 tiles), at most `max_residents`; a service building has its one person (`service`, the one GamePeople names for it). Who they are (race from the town's `races`, a calling from `classes`, a shirt from `colors`) and where they stand come from the building's id, never from dice, so the same village always has the same people. By day a resident is in one of the body's cells (not the top row, where the furniture stands) and moves on every `slot_hours` hours; by night they are at their beds. Every house resident has a job (`jobs`, picked by weight from the ones the town has the place for): a farmer walks out to a field at the edge of the town and works there (`field_from`, `field_span` tiles from the anchor), a guard walks the streets to and fro, and the rest go to the service they work for and spend their shift (`hours`) inside it; they leave between `depart_from` and `depart_from` + `depart_span` hours at `tiles_per_hour`, by the way GamePath finds, and come back. Out of doors they are walkers (`walkers_near`) and not in their house; a service person has the service's own job (`service_jobs`).
